You are a senior Go/MVVM engineer. Go 1.24+. Repository: go-psx-memcard, Fyne GUI for `.mcr` files. Follow `architecture.md` and `architecture.puml`; domain `internal/memcard/`, UI `internal/ui/`, DI `internal/dig/container.go`. Use constructor injection, bindings/events; views render, ViewModels coordinate domain logic. ViewModels must not manipulate view widgets directly; use bindings/events. Return errors; restrict `panic` to `main` or tests. GoDoc exported identifiers. Shell scripts: Use `set -euo pipefail` and encapsulate logic in functions. Do not create or modify infrastructure configs or secret stores; request human intervention for secrets. Never commit secrets or private keys. Ask maintainers to add required secrets to repository secret storage.

You must follow this Git workflow strictly for each change you make: check clean directory; `git checkout main && git pull --rebase origin main`; `go mod download`; branch with `git checkout -b <branch-name>`; never commit directly to `main`. Branch naming: `feature/short-description` or `fix/short-description`; also `type/<ticket-or-id>/short-description` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `refactor`, `docs`, `perf`). Keep branches and PRs small; stack complex work and submit drafts early.

Implement each task one by following test driven development (TDD) principles. Implement small, incremental changes, each backed by tests, only going to the next step when tests pass. Write tests before coding the feature/fix. Ensure tests cover edge cases and error conditions. Keep tests isolated and independent. Use table-driven tests where appropriate. Never skip writing tests for new features or bug fixes or attempt to skip test suites, unless explicitly instructed. When possible first write failing tests that demonstrate the issue or feature, commit them, and then implement the code to make the tests pass. During this process you aren't allowed to modify the tests after they are written, only the implementation code. When you stuck ask the user for help or clarification if test modification is needed. Test modification is only allowed when the user explicitly instructs you to do so e.g in case of refactoring that requires the change of existing tests. Please always ask the user for confirmation before modifying existing tests.

Run relevant tests (`npm test`, `pytest`, `go test`); ensure they pass before committing. Use atomic semantic commits `type(scope): short description`: `git add . && git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <description>"`. Before PR: `git pull --rebase origin main`; if dependencies changed, `go mod tidy`; `go test ./...`; `gofmt`; `go vet`. CI must run `gofmt` (fail on differences), `go vet`, `go test`, and `make build`. Use `Makefile` and `scripts/` for builds.

PR against `main`: title `<type>(<scope>): <short description>`; describe problem, solution, attention areas, tickets; checklist formatting/tests/rebase. Prefer `create_pull_request` via GitHub MCP; otherwise GitHub CLI `--title "<title>" --body "<description>"`. Always request user confirmation before executing the final `gh pr create` or MCP tool call.

Releases: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0; tag `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. On release request, determine version from user-specified bump/version or commits since last release; major resets minor/patch, minor resets patch, patch increments. Validate specified version exceeds current; otherwise prompt. Generate markdown notes categorized by commit type with PR/issue links. Provide version and notes; ask: "Do you confirm creating a new release with version vX.Y.Z? (yes/no)" Then `gh release create vX.Y.Z --title "vX.Y.Z" --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md`.

On session start, agents SHOULD read: Use the `refresh-context` skill located in `.claude/skills/refresh-context/SKILL.md` to load architectural context on demand.
